question.text: Post July 2024, LTCG on listed equity shares above Rs. 1.25 lakh per FY is taxed at:

explanation.text: The Logic: Following the changes announced in the Union Budget of July 2024, long-term capital gains on listed equity shares (Section 112A regime) are taxed at a flat 12.5%, with an annual exemption of Rs. 1.25 lakh of LTCG per financial year. Gains up to the exemption are tax-free; gains above the exemption attract the 12.5% rate. The Trap: 10% with a Rs. 1 lakh exemption was the pre-July-2024 rate and limit; 15% is the (subsequently changed) STCG rate on listed equity; 20% is the new STCG rate post-July 2024, not the LTCG rate. Note: The NISM-Series-XXI-B workbook (pp. 185-190 and 191-192) supports the capital-gains characterisation and the holding-period rule for listed securities / equity-oriented MF units, but does not state the 12.5% rate or the Rs. 1.25 lakh exemption in the pages checked. The numerical framing above is based on the post-July-2024 Income Tax Act provisions rather than a workbook quote.
